+# DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash config.json (snapshot dba1be0a): the decoder layout the spans depend on
+LAYERS = 40
+COMPRESS = [0, 0] + [2] * 18 + [1] * 20
+ENGRAM = (1, 14)
+INDEX_SOURCES = (2, 8, 14, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36)
+
+
+def _model(capture=None):
+    layers = []
+    for i in range(LAYERS):
+        source = i in INDEX_SOURCES
+        attn = types.SimpleNamespace(
+            compress_ratio=COMPRESS[i],
+            compressor=object() if source else None,
+            indexer=object() if source else None,
+        )
+        mlp = types.SimpleNamespace(is_hash=False, is_nextn=False)
+        layers.append(
+            types.SimpleNamespace(
+                hc_boundary_fused=True,
+                mlp=mlp,
+                self_attn=attn,
+                engram=object() if i in ENGRAM else None,
+            )
+        )
+    model = types.SimpleNamespace(
+        layers=layers, start_layer=0, end_layer=LAYERS, dspark_layers_to_capture=capture
+    )
+    return types.SimpleNamespace(model=model)
+
+
+def _ids(plan, name):
+    return {i for i, spans in plan.layers.items() if any(s.name == name for s in spans)}
+
+
+class TestSpans(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_decode_layer_sets(self):
+        plan = dsv41.spans(_model(), StepKind.DECODE)
+        k1, ffn = _ids(plan, "k1"), _ids(plan, "ffn")
+        self.assertEqual(ffn, set(range(LAYERS)))
+        self.assertEqual(len(k1), 30)
+        self.assertTrue(k1.isdisjoint({0, *ENGRAM, *INDEX_SOURCES}), sorted(k1))
+        for spans in plan.layers.values():
+            self.assertEqual(spans[-1], dsv41.FFN)
+
+    def test_verify_leaves_out_captured_layers(self):
+        capture = [10, 21, 33]
+        decode = _ids(dsv41.spans(_model(capture), StepKind.DECODE), "k1")
+        plan = dsv41.spans(_model(capture), StepKind.TARGET_VERIFY)
+        verify = _ids(plan, "k1")
+        self.assertEqual(verify, decode - set(capture))
+        self.assertEqual(len(verify), 27)
+        self.assertTrue(
+            any("DSpark captures" in n and "[10, 21, 33]" in n for n in plan.notes),
+            plan.notes,
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(_ids(plan, "ffn"), set(range(LAYERS)))
+
+
+def _cfg(**over):
+    fields = dict(speculative_algorithm="DSPARK", tp_size=4)
+    fields.update(over)
+    return types.SimpleNamespace(**fields)
+
+
+def _hf():
+    return types.SimpleNamespace(**dsv41._MODEL)
+
+
+class TestConfigReasons(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self):
+        envs = dsv41.envs
+        self.patches = [
+            mock.patch.object(dsv41, "is_gfx95_supported", return_value=True),
+            mock.patch.object(dsv41, "get_bool_env_var", return_value=False),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                envs.SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE, "get", return_value="static"
+            ),
+            mock.patch.object(envs.SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_EXPERTS, "get", return_value=True),
+            mock.patch.object(envs.SGLANG_DSV4_FP4_DEQUANT, "get", return_value=False),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                envs.SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV, "get", return_value=True
+            ),
+            mock.patch.object(envs.SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT, "get", return_value="v4"),
+            mock.patch.object(envs.SGLANG_TEST_MONO_SPANS, "get", return_value=""),
+        ]
+        for p in self.patches:
+            p.start()
+
+    def tearDown(self):
+        for p in self.patches:
+            p.stop()
+
+    def test_cookbook_recipe_accepted(self):
+        self.assertEqual(dsv41.config_disable_reasons(_cfg(), _hf()), [])
+        self.assertEqual(
+            dsv41.config_disable_reasons(
+                _cfg(speculative_algorithm=None, tp_size=2), _hf()
+            ),
+            [],
+        )
+
+    def test_refusals(self):
+        def one(cfg=None, hf=None):
+            reasons = dsv41.config_disable_reasons(cfg or _cfg(), hf or _hf())
+            self.assertEqual(len(reasons), 1, reasons)
+            return reasons[0]
+
+        self.assertIn("DSpark", one(_cfg(speculative_algorithm="EAGLE")))
+        self.assertIn("tensor parallel size 8", one(_cfg(tp_size=8)))
+        bad = _hf()
+        bad.n_routed_experts = 256
+        self.assertIn("n_routed_experts", one(hf=bad))
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            dsv41.envs.SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE, "get", return_value="compact"
+        ):
+            self.assertIn("SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE", one())
+        with mock.patch.object(
+            dsv41.envs.SGLANG_TEST_MONO_SPANS, "get", return_value="k1"
+        ):
+            self.assertIn("k1 needs ffn", one())
+
+    def test_every_reason_at_once(self):
+        reasons = dsv41.config_disable_reasons(
+            _cfg(speculative_algorithm="EAGLE", tp_size=8), _hf()
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(len(reasons), 2, reasons)
+
+
+def _function(path: pathlib.Path, cls: str, name: str) -> str:
+    """The source of method ``cls.name`` (or function ``name`` when cls is None), read without importing."""
+    tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if cls is None and isinstance(node, ast.FunctionDef) and node.name == name:
+            return ast.unparse(node)
+        if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and node.name == cls:
+            for item in node.body:
+                if isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef) and item.name == name:
+                    return ast.unparse(item)
+    raise LookupError(f"{cls}.{name} not in {path}")
+
+
+class TestHookPlacement(unittest.TestCase):
+    """load_tensor sees each checkpoint tensor before renames and quantization; loaded() runs at the end of
+    load_weights, before process_weights_after_loading; attach runs when the kernels are precompiled."""
+
+    def test_deepseek_v4_calls(self):
+        path = ROOT / "srt" / "models" / "deepseek_v4.py"
+        src = _function(path, "DeepseekV4ForCausalLM", "load_weights")
+        at = src.index("mono.load_tensor(")
+        self.assertLess(at, src.index("_prepare_deepseek_v4_weights("))
+        self.assertLess(at, src.index("remap_weight_name_to_dpsk_hf_format("))
+        self.assertGreater(
+            src.index("mono.loaded(self)"), src.index("self.post_load_weights(")
+        )
+        pre = _function(
+            path, "DeepseekV4ForCausalLM", "precompile_kernels_after_loading"
+        )
+        body = ast.parse(pre).body[0].body
+        self.assertEqual(ast.unparse(body[0]).strip(), "mono.attach(self)")
+
+    def test_loader_runs_post_processing_after_load_weights(self):
+        path = ROOT / "srt" / "model_loader" / "loader.py"
+        src = _function(path, "DefaultModelLoader", "load_weights_and_postprocess")
+        self.assertLess(
+            src.index("load_weights_only("), src.index("postprocess_weights(")
+        )
+        self.assertIn(
+            "process_weights_after_loading",
+            _function(path, "DefaultModelLoader", "postprocess_weights"),
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""The contract between the plugin and SGLang (RFC #43949 section 11), checked on CPU from both sides.
+
+Each plugin module lists the SGLang names it reads in ``SGLANG_READS``, by file. Every ``sglang.srt`` import of a
+plugin module must name a declared file and name, and every declared entry must still exist in that file: a plain
+name as a definition, an assignment target, an attribute assignment, a class field or an imported name; ``f(p)`` as
+function ``f`` with parameter ``p``; ``'"x"'`` as the string literal ``x``. Both sides are read from source, so the
+GPU-only kernel modules are checked without importing them."""
+
+import ast
+import pathlib
+import re
+import unittest
+
+import sglang
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=10, suite="base-a-test-cpu")
+
+ROOT = pathlib.Path(sglang.__file__).parent
+PLUGIN = ROOT / "experimental" / "monokernels"
+CALL = re.compile(r"^(\w+)\((\w+)\)$")
+LITERAL = re.compile(r'^"(.*)"$')
+
+
+def srt_key(module: str) -> str:
+    """The SGLANG_READS key of an sglang.srt module: its file relative to python/sglang."""
+    rel = pathlib.Path(*module.split(".")[1:])
+    path = ROOT / rel.with_suffix(".py")
+    if not path.exists():
+        path = ROOT / rel / "__init__.py"
+    return str(path.relative_to(ROOT)).replace("\\", "/")
+
+
+def declared_reads(tree: ast.Module) -> dict:
+    for node in tree.body:
+        if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) and any(
+            isinstance(t, ast.Name) and t.id == "SGLANG_READS" for t in node.targets
+        ):
+            return ast.literal_eval(node.value)
+    return {}
+
+
+def srt_imports(tree: ast.AST) -> dict:
+    """sglang.srt module -> names imported from it (at any depth, including lazy imports)."""
+    out = {}
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if (
+            isinstance(node, ast.ImportFrom)
+            and node.module
+            and node.module.startswith("sglang.srt")
+        ):
+            out.setdefault(node.module, set()).update(a.name for a in node.names)
+        elif isinstance(node, ast.Import):
+            for a in node.names:
+                if a.name.startswith("sglang.srt"):
+                    out.setdefault(a.name, set())
+    return out
+
+
+def defined_names(tree: ast.AST) -> set:
+    names = set()
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)):
+            names.add(node.name)
+        elif isinstance(node, (ast.Assign, ast.AugAssign, ast.AnnAssign)):
+            targets = node.targets if isinstance(node, ast.Assign) else [node.target]
+            for t in targets:
+                for sub in ast.walk(t):
+                    if isinstance(sub, ast.Name):
+                        names.add(sub.id)
+                    elif isinstance(sub, ast.Attribute):
+                        names.add(sub.attr)
+        elif isinstance(node, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):
+            for alias in node.names:
+                names.add((alias.asname or alias.name).split(".")[0])
+    return names
+
+
+def function_params(tree: ast.AST) -> dict:
+    out = {}
+    for node in ast.walk(tree):
+        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
+            a = node.args
+            out.setdefault(node.name, set()).update(
+                p.arg for p in a.posonlyargs + a.args + a.kwonlyargs
+            )
+    return out
+
+
+def string_literals(tree: ast.AST) -> set:
+    return {
+        n.value
+        for n in ast.walk(tree)
+        if isinstance(n, ast.Constant) and isinstance(n.value, str)
+    }
+
+
+def plugin_files():
+    return sorted(PLUGIN.rglob("*.py"))
+
+
+class TestSGLangReads(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_every_srt_import_is_declared(self):
+        for path in plugin_files():
+            tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
+            reads = declared_reads(tree)
+            for module, names in srt_imports(tree).items():
+                key = srt_key(module)
+                with self.subTest(file=str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), imports=module):
+                    self.assertIn(
+                        key, reads, f"imports {module} without SGLANG_READS[{key!r}]"
+                    )
+                    for n in names:
+                        self.assertIn(n, reads[key], f"reads {module}.{n} undeclared")
+
+    def test_every_declared_name_exists(self):
+        checked = 0
+        for path in plugin_files():
+            for rel, entries in declared_reads(ast.parse(path.read_text())).items():
+                target = ROOT / rel
+                with self.subTest(file=str(path.relative_to(ROOT)), reads=rel):
+                    self.assertTrue(target.exists(), f"{rel} no longer exists")
+                    tree = ast.parse(target.read_text())
+                    names, params, literals = (
+                        defined_names(tree),
+                        function_params(tree),
+                        string_literals(tree),
+                    )
+                    for entry in entries:
+                        checked += 1
+                        call, lit = CALL.match(entry), LITERAL.match(entry)
+                        if call:
+                            f, p = call.groups()
+                            self.assertIn(
+                                p, params.get(f, set()), f"{rel}: {f}({p}) is gone"
+                            )
+                        elif lit:
+                            self.assertIn(
+                                lit.group(1),
+                                literals,
+                                f"{rel}: literal {entry} is gone",
+                            )
+                        else:
+                            self.assertIn(entry, names, f"{rel}: {entry} is gone")
+        self.assertGreater(checked, 50)
+
+    def test_grammar(self):
+        tree = ast.parse(
+            "def f(a, *, b):\n    return 'x'\nclass C:\n    y: int = 0\nobj.z = 1\n"
+        )
+        self.assertEqual(function_params(tree)["f"], {"a", "b"})
+        self.assertTrue({"f", "C", "y", "z"} <= defined_names(tree))
+        self.assertIn("x", string_literals(tree))
+        self.assertEqual(CALL.match("f(b)").groups(), ("f", "b"))
+        self.assertEqual(LITERAL.match('"null"').group(1), "null")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

issue_comments.body:
A general comment: You have all the monokernel code in models/deepseek_common/amd/dsv41_mono/ - So in a vendor-specific directory under a model-specific directory. I expect we'll be seeing a lot of monokernels for AMD devices, and they will probably be based on the same flysDSL skeleton. Are there reusable parts of the code that could be placed in some shared AMD monokernel library directory? Or is the idea of monokernels that they are self-sustainable when it comes to code?

Thanks @rkarhila-amd good questions!

On the code location: AMD maintainers have been careful with PRs that touch common code, so I kept this self-contained on purpose. Apart from some minor changes in `environ.py` and `deepseek_v4.py`, it's all new code under `deepseek_common/amd/` plus tests, and it's off by default. It's the same layout vLLM merged in vllm-project/vllm#60397. The reusable part is already split out in `dsv41_mono/common/` (from ROCm/ATOM's `atom/mono`). When a second model's mono kernels come to SGLang, we can move it to a shared AMD folder in a small follow-up PR. vLLM is starting to do the same.

On other GPUs: this PR is gfx950 only and stops at startup with a clear error elsewhere, so gfx942 users see no change. gfx942 is possible but needs a port, and vLLM has a draft for it (vllm-project/vllm#60731). With 64 KB of LDS instead of 160 KB, it takes up to 42 rows instead of 48, runs at TP4 only and adds a few kernels. We can bring it over as a follow-up PR. For gfx1250, I'd wait: these kernels are built for fixed shapes and tuned per chip, so a small separate PR once the hardware and FlyDSL support are ready is cleaner.

Update: SGLang now runs DeepSeek-V4.1 monokernels through the sgl-amd-mono plugin (`--monokernel-backend amd`, #44353). We compared this PR with the plugin's `deepseek_v41`, and sent the parts the plugin does not have yet to sgl-amd-mono:

- sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#<N1>: the FFN seam builds its residual with SGLang's arithmetic, as the K1 seam already does. The residual now matches SGLang's bit for bit at all 48 widths, at TP2 and TP4, with no measurable change in launch time.
- sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#<N2>: the kernel checks test every width the spec builds. This check found the FFN seam deviation at TP4.
- sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#<N3>: the graph checks fail on allocator growth during capture or replay.
- sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#<N4>: a fault on one rank must stop every rank, tested with one process per rank.
- sgl-project/sgl-amd-mono#<N5>: the e2e fault test passes on ROCm 7.2 images, which report the fault without an address.

This draft stays open as the record of our in-tree work. It is not for merge.
